Story & Plot

Created by inventor Geppetto and influenced by a sinister Cricket voiced by Robert Englund, Pinocchio embarks on a violent crusade to carve himself into a real boy like his brother James, one piece at a time. The setting takes place in an English countryside estate where Geppetto lives with his preteen grandson James. The public-domain slasher horror twists a beloved children's classic into a sick serial killer story.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film leans into campy absurdity, balancing brutal gore with a darkly hilarious horror romp that twists a children's classic. It offers a low-budget, high-concept entertainment value relying on its bizarre premise rather than traditional witty banter. Reviewers note its campy nature, though it remains a twisted kidlit spin.

Performances & Direction

Richard Brake brings real menace as the inventor Geppetto, anchoring the film with a strong screen presence. Robert Englund delivers a fun, weird touch voicing the sinister Cricket. Cameron Bell appears as James, rounding out the core cast alongside Jude Evan Lloyd, Jessica Balmer, and Jack Art Gray.

Strengths

  • impressive practical effects
  • killer puppetry
  • strong atmosphere
  • Richard Brake's menacing performance
  • unsettling kill concept

Weaknesses

The film is narratively anemic and thin on story, feeling clearly rushed at 82 minutes. It is never especially frightening, with jump scares that are oddly muffled, and it suffers from a familiar setup as a public-domain horror cash-in.

Final verdict

Pinocchio: Unstrung is a surprisingly effective horror adaptation for fans of trashy, low-budget slashers. A determined man embarks on a high-stakes quest to fulfill his dream of being the first to reach the summit of Mount Everest. Comedy & Entertainment

As a biographical drama focused on historical mountain climbing and severe hardship, the film does not rely on traditional humor for its entertainment value.
